main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling devil curry in the shared kitchen, given smell in the living room, bedrooms and laundry.

A-B.evidence: A asked for no smelly cooking (T1) and B agreed (T2); A accepted the after-7pm plan (T13), while B accepted only a once-a-week plan with warning (T19) and raised laundry concerns (T27).

A-C.evidence: C backed A's complaint (T3); A accepted the after-7pm plan (T13), while C kept raising laundry problems (T21, T28) and never accepted any plan.

A-D.evidence: A asked for a ban and D defended the food (T4-5); D offered cooking after 7pm with a heads-up (T12) and A said 'that works for me' (T13). A mentioned being out on Saturdays (T26) and D proposed Saturday evenings (T29).

B-C.evidence: B and C both object to smell in the room and laundry (T8-9); B backs C on dampness: 'She's right' (T23).

B-D.evidence: B rejects the plan (T16); D offers once a week (T17); B accepts with the door shut and a warning (T19) and D agrees (T20); B then raises the laundry problem (T23) and D responds (T25).

C-D.evidence: C objects to the smell on laundry (T3); D accommodates by asking about laundry times (T25, T29) after C rejects bringing laundry in (T21), but C has not accepted the Saturday proposal.
